newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI aims for 30 bln yen sales from Internet access.
newsitem.headline: DDI aims for 30 bln yen sales from Internet access.

text.p: Japan's phone operator DDI Corp said on Monday that it aims for annual sales of 30 billion yen from its new Internet access service in the 1999/2000 fiscal year.
DDI will start offering the Internet access service to corporate users on July 1 and to individual users from the autumn.

"We hope to acquire at least a five percent share of the market, which is estimated to grow to around 600 billion yen in 1999/2000," Tadashi Onodera, executive vice president of DDI, told a news conference.

The new service, called DDI Integrated Open Network (DION), will allow corporate users to access the Internet using 128 kilobit dedicated lines at 24,000 yen a month, cheaper than similar services offered by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and Japan Telecom Co, Onodera said.
DDI will also help corporate customers build local area networks using the Internet under the DION service.
Onodera said DDI plans to differentiate its services from rivals by offering necessary products, contents and services in one package.
